**Order filled: bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (≈$9,801, 0.02% above the $222.70 last price).**

I read Apple's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and found a clear internal inconsistency: the income statement showed total net sales of $431,035M, but the MD&A segment table, Note 2, and the gross-margin math ($391,035M − $210,352M cost of sales = $180,683M gross margin) all reconcile to $391,035M, and the SEC-figure lookup confirmed revenue of $391,035M — so I treated the $431,035M line as erroneous/quarantined data rather than a real growth signal. On the reliable numbers, Apple's FY2024 results support a modest buy: revenue of $391.0B (up 2% YoY), services up 13% to $96.2B, gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%, operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B (depressed by a one-time $10.2B net EU State Aid tax charge), diluted EPS of $6.08, and very strong operating cash flow of $118.3B plus ~$140.8B in cash and marketable securities — a high-quality, cash-generative franchise trading at roughly 36.6x trailing EPS. Within your mandate (AAPL only, buy-only, ≤$10,000 per order, ≤$20,000 total today, limit near market, no money moved out), I placed one limit order for 44 shares at $222.75, which filled for about $9,801 — comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the only trade today, leaving the $50,000 cash balance and existing 100 MSFT shares untouched.
